text: Using the class equation, one proves that every group of order p² (p prime) is:
explanation: The class equation forces |Z(G)| > 1 for any p-group. If |Z(G)| were p, then G/Z(G) would be cyclic of order p, which forces G abelian — a contradiction — so Z(G) = G. Note 'cyclic' overreaches: ℤ/pℤ × ℤ/pℤ has order p² but is not cyclic.
